title: Bounded noise changes reverse lag signs in reciprocal models of two adult worm electrical maps
abstract: We tested whether unequal independent noise gives directional lag correlations in passive models with reciprocal electrical coupling. Two partial adult worm maps gave 180 cells and 262 or 296 direct pairs. At lag 0.1 and a source variance ratio bounded by two, the median share of direct pairs with an absolute lag-correlation difference above 0.01 was 14.9% and 12.8% across 100 declared noise patterns. Reflecting each noise variance rate about one reverses every nonzero lag sign without changing wiring. A Lyapunov identity proves this reversal for any symmetric positive definite drift and any observed subset. Equal noise gave numerical zero. Independent matrix calculations and a two-cell formula passed. The general time irreversibility theory is established; this report adds a bounded-noise construction and a map-based size benchmark. These are exact population model results. Missing electrical annotations, assumed conductances and noise, and the absence of measured activity or finite-record tests prevent a biological direction claim.

display.caption: Unequal source noise gives lag asymmetry with reciprocal wiring. Lines show medians and shading shows the 5th to 95th percentiles of 100 model noise patterns. Coupling scale is one. These are model ranges, not animal confidence intervals.
